newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Bezeq end squabble over tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Bezeq end squabble over tariffs.

text.p: The Israeli government and Bezeq Israel Telecom said on Sunday they had ended their overseas dialling rates squabble, opening the way for the start of competition in Israel's international calls market.

"I accepted the tariffs Bezeq International decided upon," Communications Minister Limor Livnat said, a week after accusing the subsidiary of the state-owned telecommunications company of setting "dumping prices" for overseas calls.
"I have the authority to set...minimum and maximum prices for Bezeq International. As things stand now, I did not find it necessary to do so," she told a news conference.
Livnat said Bezeq is expected by Monday to complete hooking up the new international calling providers Barak and Golden Lines and predicted "sharp and tough competition".
A spokesman for Bezeq Israel Telecom, said Bezeq International had agreed the tariffs at a board meeting late on Saturday and the dispute was over.
He said only "small changes" were made to the rates Livnat had earlier opposed, which means that Bezeq's overseas tariffs would be about 80 percent less than what it currently charges.

Calling her price supervisory powers a "safety net", Livnat said: "If within four months it becomes clear Bezeq International has more than 90 percent of the market, I have the legal authority to raise its tariffs."
But, she said, if Bezeq's market share drops to 80 percent within three months, she will allow the company to set lower overseas charges.
Golden Lines is controlled by SBC Communications Inc, Italy's Stet and three Israeli partners.
Barak is controlled by Sprint Corp, France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom, Clal Israel and Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.

A rate schedule distributed at the news conference by the Communications Ministry showed the average cost of a call to the United States dropping from around 3.50 shekels a minute to 0.77 at Bezeq, 0.72 at Golden Lines and 0.69 at Barak.
